A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same collective counterfactual explanation research, despite the changed title and substantial reformulation. Their main texts, equations, figures, algorithms, and appendices are available and readable, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B.4 report original Gaussian-mixture simulations comparing classical CE with optimal-transport approaches, including regularization tradeoffs and transport trajectories.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original experiments on Adult, COMPAS, HELOC, and Moons, including baseline comparisons, sensitivity results, and recourse visualizations.

M1.justification: v1 centers CCE on transport to a fixed δ-confidence distribution, with a KL-penalized unbalanced variant. v2 replaces this with a population-equilibrium objective penalizing χ² divergence from the positive-class distribution, incorporates partial compliance, and adds projected-gradient and entropy-based solvers. The path-guided and ordered-classifier formulations also change; the utility-based extension is removed.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates a two-dimensional Gaussian mixture with three prescribed classifier boundaries. Those simulations are replaced by Adult, COMPAS, HELOC, and Moons in v2, substantially expanding represented domains to real datasets. Recourse evaluation remains restricted to two selected features per dataset.

E2.justification: v1 compares classical nearest-point CE with balanced and unbalanced OT variants. v2 Figure 4 evaluates a substantially broader recourse comparator set: Wachter, Growing Spheres, CLUE, FOCUS, C-CHVAE, and ROAR. ROAR appears for Adult, COMPAS, and Moons, but is absent from the HELOC comparison.

E3.justification: v1 uses 100 synthetic samples, prescribed classifiers, and δ=0.2. v2 introduces 80/20 training/test splits, MLP or random-forest predictors, and 1,000 instances per class for the new benchmarks. Evaluation adds grid-based, weighted χ² competition cost and combined cost, replacing the earlier KL target-mismatch analysis. These are new experimental protocols, not comparable reruns of v1.

E4.justification: The central sensitivity question remains the tradeoff between modification cost and distribution matching. v1's KL-based λ2 sweeps over [0,1] and boundary-specific Gaussian examples are replaced by a χ²-based sweep over [0.01,0.3] in v2 Figure 5, alongside revised trajectory and recourse illustrations. This updates existing analysis questions without adding a distinct systematic robustness or component-ablation investigation.

E5.justification: v1 reports no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 reports 100 experiments with different random seeds, means and standard-deviation bars in Figure 4, and confidence intervals in Figure 5. This introduces uncertainty reporting across the empirical study; the confidence-interval level and construction are unspecified.

E6.justification: The Gaussian-mixture cost curves and transport results are replaced by new benchmark and visualization results. v2 Figure 4 reports the lowest competition and combined costs for CCE across the four datasets, while its modification cost is not lowest. These findings concern changed datasets, objectives, and protocols and therefore do not establish a same-setting performance improvement over v1.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a population-dynamics PDE, equilibrium and compliance assumptions, a measurable-selection lemma, the χ² mixture identity, and propositions on relaxed-plan existence, consistency, and computational complexity, with derivations and proofs in Appendices C–D. Several earlier CCE map guarantees and the utility-based derivation disappear. Much of the generic OT background is retained in Appendix B rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes density-guided OT recommendations, a market interpretation of modification cost, and CE desiderata. v2 makes population-dynamics modeling, explicit competition penalties, guarantees for an unbalanced relaxation, and comparative empirical effectiveness central contributions. The collective-recourse goal persists, but the claimed scientific contribution is substantially redefined.

C2.justification: The loan-intermediation and utility interpretations in v1 give way to resource scarcity and deviations from population equilibrium in v2. New qualifications address fixed resources, partial compliance, unmodeled strategic deviations, and application-specific competition weights. Causality changes from deferred work to a proposed connection through causal metrics, although full integration remains deferred.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's synthetic-data parameters and OT pseudocode, v2 documents CARLA usage, selected dataset features, baseline hyperparameters and VAE configurations in Table 1, and the new solvers' update rules. It also supplies a back-and-forth implementation link and promises experimental code after review; it does not establish that this code is already available.

R1.justification: v2 retains the earlier distribution-aware and collective-CE comparisons but substantially expands positioning around group counterfactuals, strategic classification, externalities, and mean-field population dynamics. Section 6 adds several group-CE approaches and explicitly distinguishes social-welfare optimization from modeling strategic deviations. Novelty is repositioned around population dynamics.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and substantial portions of the methodological narrative are rewritten. The OT overview moves from main-text Section 2 to Appendix B, related work moves from Section 1.2 to Section 6, and computational exposition becomes a dedicated numerical-study section. The appendices are reorganized around definitions, background, population dynamics, proofs, algorithms, and experiments.

P2.justification: The Gaussian-density illustrations and simulation panels are replaced by redrawn Moons illustrations, a multi-dataset bar-chart comparison with error bars, a combined sensitivity/Adult figure, and HELOC/COMPAS recourse panels. v2 adds a baseline-hyperparameter table and removes the earlier notation table. These substantially redesign the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly deferred real-data evaluation and formal externality modeling. v2 addresses both with an explicit population model and broader baseline comparisons, supported by 100-seed uncertainty reporting and implementation details. This substantially strengthens the paper's empirical support and transparency. Two-feature evaluation and deferred code release limit practical conclusions, and Appendix D.5 describes a normalization step absent from Algorithm 1, so the added technical material still needs reconciliation.
